definition: The rule that expands $(a + b)^{n}$, for $n \in \mathbb{N}$, as the sum of the terms ${}^{n}C_{r}\,a^{n-r}b^{r}$ for $r = 0, 1, \dots, n$.
The number ${}^{n}C_{r} = \frac{n!}{r!\,(n-r)!}$: the number of ways to choose $r$ objects from $n$, and the coefficient of $a^{n-r}b^{r}$ in $(a + b)^{n}$.
A triangle of numbers in which each entry is the sum of the two above it; row $n$, counted from row $0$, gives the coefficients of $(a + b)^{n}$.
For a whole number $n \ge 1$, $n!$ is the product $n \times (n - 1) \times \dots \times 2 \times 1$; by definition $0! = 1$.
The term of an expression with no power of the variable in it, that is, the term in $x^{0}$.
